items.title: Understanding the Difference Between Weather and Climate
items.explanation: 'Weather' refers to short-term atmospheric conditions like rain, sunshine, or wind that change from hour to hour. 'Climate' is the long-term pattern of weather in a specific region over several decades. In India, while daily weather varies, the climate is defined by recurring seasonal patterns such as the monsoon.

items.title: The Four Main Seasons Across Most Regions
items.explanation: Most regions experience four main seasons: spring, summer, autumn, and winter. However, India receives rainfall during a specific period called the 'rainy season' or monsoon, alongside these other four seasons.

items.title: Traditional Six Seasons of India
items.explanation: Traditionally, in many parts of India, the year is divided into six seasons known as ritus: vasanta (spring), griṣhma (summer), varṣha (rainy season), s̄harad (autumn), hemanta (pre-winter), and s̄his̄hir (winter). These are associated with specific rituals and festivals.

items.title: Climate Stability vs. Change
items.explanation: Usually, the climate remains stable over long periods of time. However, scientists have recorded changes in global climates in recent decades, often caused by human actions.
